x: Apart from the group in the lead the others were strung out, in some cases very widely. At the finish Bert Footer came in an easy winner by about 50 yds., with J. Flower and Allum filling 2nd and 3rd places.

When the field was sighted, for the turn home, Carter was leading the pack, running comfortably, followed by Ring, Shields, Rice, and J. Flower, with our "South of the Thames" Juniors, Martin, Saunders and Chantler, close on their heels.

Patience 12th, Smart 23rd, J. Flower 28th, Shields 33rd—very satisfactory for the half-way stage. 85 points for 6—with another close up—was very cheering indeed, and they kept these position round the field and so out again into the woods.
